s1.syndrome_frame: chronic lump and pain at the posterior aspect of the knee joint
salient_findings: 3-year history of a lump on the posterior aspect of the right knee joint
pain and discomfort while walking or standing with the knee joint extended
3 x 3 cm sized palpable lump at posterior aspect of right knee joint
key_facts: 53-year-old woman
3-year history of a lump on the posterior aspect of the right knee joint
no underlying diseases
pain and discomfort while walking or standing with the knee joint extended
range of right knee motion (ROM): 10-130°
no internal swelling of the knee joint
no tenderness of medial or lateral joint line
normal Lachman test results
normal valgus and varus stress tests
3 x 3 cm sized palpable lump at posterior aspect of right knee joint
mild osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1) in both knee joints
multi-lobulated cyst measuring 3.3 cm × 3.0 cm × 3.9 cm at popliteal fossa

shortlist.label: Baker's cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Multi-lobulated cyst at popliteal fossa, consistent with Baker's cyst

shortlist.label: Popliteal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cyst located at posterior aspect of knee joint, similar to popliteal cyst

shortlist.label: Ganglion cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Palpable lump at posterior aspect of knee joint, possible ganglion cyst

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: 3 x 3 cm sized palpable lump, could be a lipoma

shortlist.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
shortlist.why_kept: Mild osteoarthritis and joint lump, possible PVNS

raw.rationale: The presence of a multi-lobulated cyst at the popliteal fossa, along with mild osteoarthritis, is consistent with a Baker's cyst, which is a type of cyst that occurs in the popliteal fossa and is often associated with osteoarthritis.

rejected.label: Popliteal cyst
rejected.why: While the location is consistent, 'popliteal cyst' is a more general term and 'Baker's cyst' is a specific diagnosis that better explains the association with osteoarthritis.

rejected.label: Ganglion cyst
rejected.why: Ganglion cysts are typically smaller and more superficial, and are not as commonly associated with osteoarthritis as Baker's cysts.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: The MRI findings do not suggest a lipoma, which would be a fatty tumor, rather than a fluid-filled cyst.

rejected.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with joint swelling, pain, and stiffness, and is not as well-explained by the presence of a discrete cyst as Baker's cyst is.
